question: Ritik and Sanjay together invested ₹79,200 in a business. At the end of the year, out of a total profit of ₹16,500, Sanjay's share was ₹3,600. What was the difference between their investments?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit ratio of Ritik to Sanjay = (16500 − 3600) : 3600 = 12900 : 3600 = 43 : 12

Investment ratio is the same as the profit ratio = 43 : 12 (since time is constant).

Difference in ratio parts = 43 − 12 = 31 parts, and total = 55 parts.

Investment difference = (31 ÷ 55) × 79200 = 31 × 1440 = 44640

**∴ The correct answer is ₹44,640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Total investment = ₹79,200

⇒ Total profit = ₹16,500

⇒ Sanjay's profit = ₹3,600

⇒ Ritik's profit = ₹16,500 − ₹3,600 = ₹12,900

**Formula Used:**

⇒ Profit Ratio = Investment Ratio (when the time period is constant)

⇒ Required Value = (Ratio Difference ÷ Total Ratio) × Total Value

 
 
 Total Investment = ₹79,200 (55 Ratio Parts)

 
 
 Ritik: ₹12,900 Profit (43 parts)

 
 
 S: 12 parts

 
 
• 
 
• 
 
• 
 Investment Difference = 31 Ratio Parts
 31 × (79200 ÷ 55) = ₹44,640

**Calculations:**

⇒ Profit ratio (Ritik : Sanjay) = 12900 : 3600

⇒ Profit ratio simplified = 129 : 36 = 43 : 12

⇒ Sum of ratio parts = 43 + 12 = 55

⇒ Value of 55 parts = ₹79,200

⇒ Value of 1 part = 79200 ÷ 55 = ₹1,440

⇒ Difference in parts = 43 − 12 = 31

⇒ Difference in investment = 31 × 1440

⇒ Difference in investment = ₹44,640

**∴ The correct answer is ₹44,640.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Partnership for Same Time Period

When investments are made for the exact same duration, the total profit is distributed exactly in the ratio of their capital investments. Profit Ratio = Investment Ratio.

Partnership for Different Time Periods

When time periods differ, profit is distributed based on the product of investment and time. Profit Ratio = (Capital₁ × Time₁) : (Capital₂ × Time₂).

Active and Sleeping Partners

An active partner is paid a fixed salary or commission from the total profit for managing the business. The remaining profit is then divided according to their equivalent investment ratios.
